description:
On 2026-10-08 the host load average reached 13 while four `benchbox-comment-policy-*` Python processes, each running from its own freshly created temp venv, held about 80% CPU apiece. A timed benchmark run needs a 1-minute load below 2.0 and no other process above 50% CPU, so these runs repeatedly made the machine non-quiet; load was still 4 to 6 hours later.

Measured on 2026-10-09 (acceptance 1 and 2 of the original item are met):
- Launchers: the pre-commit hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml:9, `run_comment_policy.py --staged`) and `make comment-policy-check` (Makefile:446), which `make lint` (Makefile:410) and `ci-lint` (Makefile:613, 635) also call.
- One transition-mode run for a one-commit diff: 358 s wall, 276 s user plus 44 s sys CPU, 476 MB peak RSS, 5,768 files scanned (host load 13-19 on 10 cores).
- Cause: the run re-scans every completed scope at both head and base (scripts/check_comment_policy.py:395-398 and 418-423), not the venv.

What remains is to reduce that per-run cost.
